# Identifying Stream Typologies

## 1. Isolating Flowing Tributaries

To start from here, import the Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_2.xlsx in the Exploratory Data Analysis folder

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/1. Spatial Assessment/Data/Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_2.xlsx")

head(dat)
```

Ensure the structure looks right

```{r}
str(dat)
```

Since we are only conducting the PCA and cluster analysis on flowing tributaries, we'll isolate these observations by excluding observations from EFPC main stem and pooled non-perennial sites

```{r}
library(dplyr)

flowing_tribs<-dat %>% 
  filter(Type != "Main Stem", Flow_state != "Pooled")

head(flowing_tribs)
```

Save results to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Create a new workbook for flowing tributary sites
wb <- createWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Dat" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Dat")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Dat", flowing_tribs)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 2. Select Variables

Scaled log-transformed variables

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Variables to select
vars_to_select <- c("log_Temp_C_std", "pH_std", "log_DOC_uM_std",
                    "log_DIC_uM_std", "log_Cl_uM_std", "log_Ca_uM_std", 
                    "log_Mg_uM_std", "log_SO4_uM_std", "log_Na_uM_std", 
                    "log_K_uM_std")

# Subset flowing_tribs
scaled_blm_predict <- flowing_tribs %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(vars_to_select))

# Peek
head(scaled_blm_predict)
```

### a. Normality Checks

```{r}
# load packages
library(purrr)
library(broom)  # for tidying test outputs

# Shapiro-Wilk test for each variable in scaled_blm_predict
norm_checks_flowing_tribs <- scaled_blm_predict %>%
  map_dfr(~ broom::tidy(shapiro.test(.x)), .id = "variable") %>%
  mutate(normality = ifelse(p.value > 0.05, "Pass", "Fail"))

# View results
norm_checks_flowing_tribs
```

Save results to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Norm Checks" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Norm Checks")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Norm Checks", norm_checks_flowing_tribs)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### b. Residual Plots

```{r}
# QQ plots

# Load libraries

library(tidyr)

dr_long <- scaled_blm_predict %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")

ggplot(dr_long, aes(sample = value)) +
```

### c. Spearman Correlation Matrix

Most are still not Normally distributed, therefore we'll perform a Spearman correlation matrix prior to the PCA

```{r}
# Spearman correlation matrix on scaled log BLM predictors
cor_matrix_f_tribs <- cor(scaled_blm_predict, method = "spearman")

# Load library
library(corrplot)

# Half heatmap (lower triangle)
corrplot(cor_matrix_f_tribs,
         method = "color",
         type = "lower",         # show only the lower triangle
         tl.cex = 0.7,
         tl.col = "black",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.6)
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Create the sheet if it doesn't already exist
if(!"Spear Cor" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Spear Cor")
}

# Write your new table (example: anova_results)
writeData(wb, "Spear Cor", cor_matrix_f_tribs)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### d. **KMO Adequacy Test**

To determine whether a PCA is appropriate, we'll conduct a KMO adequacy test on all scaled log BLM predictors. It's generally accepted that

-   KMO \> 0.90 is superb

-   KMO 0.80-0.90 is great

-   KMO 0.70-0.80 is good

-   KMO 0.50-0.70 is mediocre

-   KMO \<0.50 is unaccepatable

```{r}
library(psych)  

# Scaled predictors
KMO(scaled_blm_predict)
```

The Overall MSA for scaled log-transformed BLM predictors is mediocre.

To see if removing highly correlated predictors can help, we'll omit DIC and Na:

```{r}
scaled_blm_predict$log_DIC_uM_std <- NULL
scaled_blm_predict$log_Na_uM_std <- NULL

library(psych)  

# Scaled predictors
KMO(scaled_blm_predict)
```

Overall MSA was worse, so we will keep all predictors.

## 3. PCA

Conduct PCA and view the variance explained by each principal component

```{r}
pca_result <- prcomp(scaled_blm_predict, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

summary(pca_result)  
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"PCA Results" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "PCA Results")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "PCA Results", pca_result)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

PCA plots

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(factoextra)
library(patchwork)

# Scree plot
screeplot <- fviz_eig(pca_result) + 
  labs(title = "Scree Plot of PCA for Flowing Tributaries", 
       y = "Explained variance (%)")
screeplot

# Biplot
biplot <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
             col.var = "contrib",
             repel = TRUE) +   # avoid overlapping / cutting off labels
  labs(title = "PCA on Spearman Corr Matrix for Flowing Tribs", 
       x = "PC 1 (40.7%)", 
       y = "PC 2 (18.4%)") +
  theme_minimal()
biplot

# Variance on PC1
p1 <- fviz_contrib(pca_result, choice = "var", axes = 1, top = 6) +
  labs(title = "PC 1")+
  ylim(0, 50)

# Variance on PC2
p2 <- fviz_contrib(pca_result, choice = "var", axes = 2, top = 6) +
  labs(title = "PC 2")+
  ylim(0, 50)

# Combine PC1 and PC2 plots onto one pane (2x2 layout)
top_contrib <- (p1 | p2) + plot_annotation(title = "Top Contributors for PCs 1 & 2 for Flowing Tributaries")

top_contrib
```

Save plots

```{r}
ggsave("Plots of All Flowing Tribs (pre-Typology)/Biplot.png", plot = biplot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = "print")

ggsave("Plots of All Flowing Tribs (pre-Typology)/Top_Contrib_by_PC.png", plot = top_contrib, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = "print")
```

Now that we've conducted a PCA on flowing tributaries, we can conduct a cluster analysis

## 4. Cluster Analysis of Flowing Tributaries

Justification for using K means clustering method is explained in the manuscript.

K means clustering is an unsupervised machine learning algorithm (MLA) that partitions the dataset into a predetermined number of clusters where each data point belongs to the cluster with the nearest centroid.

The number of clusters must be chosen to run K means, which can be determined by the elbow point in the PCA scree plot (in our case, 2).

The MLA randomly begins at different initial centroids (initialization), thus the results differ from run to run. To ensure the same sequence of “random” centroid selections, we set the seed at 123 to ensure reproducibility.

We chose an arbitrary number of 50 runs from which the solution with the lowest within-cluster sum of squares was chosen.

The results will assign a 1 or 2 to each observation which corresponds to the cluster it was assigned to.

```{r}
# Run k-means
set.seed(123)
kmeans_result <- kmeans(scaled_blm_predict, centers = 2, nstart = 50)

# Add cluster labels to your data
flowing_tribs <- flowing_tribs %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster))

# Check
str(flowing_tribs$cluster)
```

If the PCA object has not been created - run this

```{r}
pca_result <- prcomp(scaled_blm_predict, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

summary(pca_result) 
```

Overlay the clusters on the PCA biplot of flowing tributaries

```{r}
# First assign factor levels
flowing_tribs$cluster <- factor(flowing_tribs$cluster, levels = c("1", "2"))

library(factoextra)

pca_cluster <- fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_result,
  geom.ind    = "point",                      # points for sites
  col.var     = "black",                      # arrows in black
  habillage   = flowing_tribs$cluster,  # color by cluster
  addEllipses = TRUE,                         # cluster ellipses
  palette     = c("#D55E00", "#56B4E9"),      # one color per cluster
  legend.title = "Cluster"
) +
  labs(title = "PCA Biplot of Flowing Tribs by Cluster")

pca_cluster

```

Save plot

```{r}
ggsave("Plots of All Flowing Tribs (pre-Typology)/PCA_by_Cluster.png", plot = pca_cluster, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = "print")
```

## 5. Characterizing Clusters

First, factorize the clusters

```{r}
# Development: from low to high
dat$Development <- factor(dat$Development, 
                          levels = c("Low",
                                     "Medium",
                                     "High"))

# Drainage area: from small to large
dat$Drainage_area <- factor(dat$Drainage_area, 
                            levels = c("<0.94 km2", 
                                       "0.94-11.81 km2", 
                                       ">11.81 km2"))

# Orientation: from North to South
dat$Orientation <- factor(dat$Orientation,
                          levels = c("North slope",
                                     "Main stem",
                                     "South slope"))

# Distance from main stem: from close to far
dat$Distance_from_EFPC <- factor(dat$Distance_from_EFPC,
                                 levels = c("Main stem",
                                 "<0.22 km",
                                 "0.22-0.99 km",
                                 ">0.99 km"))

# Relative elevation: from low to high
dat$Relative_elevation <- factor(dat$Relative_elevation,
                                 levels = c(
                                   "0 m",
                                   "<2.1 m",
                                   "2.1-10.5 m",
                                   ">10.5 m"))

# Checks
levels(dat$Development)
levels(dat$Drainage_area)
levels(dat$Orientation)
levels(dat$Distance_from_EFPC)
levels(dat$Relative_elevation)
```

### a. Relative Frequency by Inherent Characteristics

Frequency table by inherent characteristics (Variable)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# inherent characteristics 
site_char <- c("Regime", "Development", "Orientation", "Distance_from_EFPC", "Drainage_area", "Relative_elevation")

cluster_summary_table_pct <- flowing_tribs %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(site_char), cluster) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -cluster,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"                            
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, cluster, Value, name = "Freq") %>% 
  group_by(Variable, cluster) %>%                  
  mutate(RelFreq = prop.table(Freq) * 100)         

cluster_summary_table_pct
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Freq by Clust" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Freq by Clust")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Freq by Clust", cluster_summary_table_pct)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

Now we'll visualize these as frequency plots of stream inherent characteristics by cluster

```{r}
library(dplyr)
# Combine variable and value
cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_summary_table_pct %>%
  mutate(Value_labeled = paste0(Variable, ": ", Value))

# Change the order of Variable Values
cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled,
  levels = c(
    # Development
    "Development: Low",
    "Development: Medium",
    "Development: High",
    
    # Distance_from_EFPC
    "Distance_from_EFPC: <0.22 km",
    "Distance_from_EFPC: 0.22-0.99 km",
    "Distance_from_EFPC: >0.99 km",
    
    # Drainage_area
    "Drainage_area: <0.94 km2",
    "Drainage_area: 0.94-11.81 km2",
    "Drainage_area: >11.81 km2",
    
    # Relative_elevation
    "Relative_elevation: <2.1 m",
    "Relative_elevation: 2.1-10.5 m",
    "Relative_elevation: >10.5 m",
    
    # Orientation
    "Orientation: North slope",
    "Orientation: South slope",
    
    # Regime
    "Regime: NonPerennial",
    "Regime: Perennial"
  )
)


# Create a named color vector for all Value_labeled combinations
color_map <- c(
  # Development
  "Development: Low" = "#fdd49e",
  "Development: Medium" = "orange2",
  "Development: High" = "red3",
  
  # Distance_from_EFPC
  "Distance_from_EFPC: <0.22 km" = "#d9f0d3",
  "Distance_from_EFPC: 0.22-0.99 km" = "#a6d854",
  "Distance_from_EFPC: >0.99 km" = "#1b7837",
  
  # Drainage_area
  "Drainage_area: <0.94 km2" = "#c8b69e",
  "Drainage_area: 0.94-11.81 km2" = "#a6761f",
  "Drainage_area: >11.81 km2" = "#543005",
  
  # Relative_elevation
  "Relative_elevation: <2.1 m" = "#dadaeb",
  "Relative_elevation: 2.1-10.5 m" = "#bcbddc",
  "Relative_elevation: >10.5 m" = "#756bb1",
  
  # Orientation
  "Orientation: North slope" = "lightgray",
  "Orientation: South slope" = "#636363",
  
  # Regime
  "Regime: NonPerennial" = "#4fb6e4",
  "Regime: Perennial" = "#1f78a4"
)

# Plot
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

rel_freq <- ggplot(cluster_summary_table_pct, 
       aes(y = Variable, x = RelFreq, fill = Value_labeled)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Relative Frequency (%)", y = NULL, fill = "Category") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
  strip.placement = "outside",
  strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
  panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
  legend.position = "right",        # move to right
  legend.box = "vertical",          # keep vertical layout
  legend.direction = "vertical"     # vertical legend
) +
guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) + # 1 column
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_map)

rel_freq
```

Save plot

```{r}
ggsave("Plots of All Flowing Tribs (pre-Typology)/Relative_Freq_Plot_by_Cluster.png", plot = rel_freq, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = "print")
```

### b. Naming Clusters

Based on these frequency plots, we were able to characterize each cluster. So we'll rename each cluster according to its defining inherent characteristics:

-   Cluster 1 will be called perennial developed flowing tributaries

-   Cluster 2 was not very distinct, both perennial and non-perennial and moderate-less developed; thus we'll refer to them as other flowing tributaries

```{r}
library(dplyr)

flowing_tribs <- flowing_tribs %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster)) %>%
  mutate(cluster = dplyr::recode(
    cluster,
    `1` = "Developed Tributaries",
    `2` = "Tributaries"
  )) %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(cluster)) %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, everything())

# check
levels(flowing_tribs$cluster)
```

Save to excel

```{r}
# Save to excel, overwrite Dat tab
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx")

# Overwrite Dat tab to include data with cluster column
writeData(wb, "Dat", flowing_tribs)

# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_flowing_tribs.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### c. Assign Typological Classification

We've established 4 distinct stream typologies:

-   Perennial developed flowing tributaries (Cluster 1)

-   All other flowing tributaries (Cluster 2)

-   3rd order EFPC main stem

-   Non-perennial pooled tributaries

Merge the cluster column from flowing_tribs into dat

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(
    flowing_tribs %>% dplyr::select(Sample_ID, cluster),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, everything()) # move cluster to first column

# check
head(dat)
```

Now add labels for the main stem and pooled non-perennial sites

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Assign labels accordingly
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(cluster = case_when(
    Type == "Main Stem" ~ "Main Stem",
    Flow_state == "Pooled" ~ "Pooled Water",
    TRUE ~ as.character(cluster) 
    ))

# Check
sum(is.na(dat$cluster)) # should be none
unique(dat$cluster)
```

Change the name from cluster to Typology and assign levels

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Rename to typology
dat <- dat %>% rename(Typology = cluster)

# Change to factor with different levels
dat$Typology <- as.factor(dat$Typology)
dat$Typology <- factor(dat$Typology, levels = c("Main Stem", 
                                              "Developed Tributaries",
                                              "Tributaries",
                                              "Pooled Water"))

# check
levels(dat$Typology)
```

Save as Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_3.xlsx in our current working directory

```{r}
                shape.ind = 16,              # all circles
                addEllipses = TRUE,
                legend.title = "Stream Typology",
                col.var = "black",
                repel = TRUE,
                label = "var"                # label the variables
) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +      # custom colors for points and ellipses
  scale_fill_manual(values = typology_colors) +       # ensures ellipses match same colors
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(16, length(unique(dat$Typology)))) +
  labs(title = "PCA on BLM Predictors: Sites Grouped by Typology") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-12, 12), ylim = c(-6, 6)) +
  theme_minimal() 

# View
pca_all_dat
```

# Identifying Important Predictors of Bioavailability

To determine the relative importance of each BLM predictor on Zn and Cu bioavailability, we will conduct separate multiple linear regressions (MLR) and use step wise selection of the most important predictors.

First, we'll import the Typology tab within the Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_3.xlsx and name it dat:

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_3.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

head(dat)
```

## 1. Check of assumptions

1.  Linear relationship between dependent and independent variables
2.  No multicollinearity among independent variables
3.  Homoscedasticity: constant variance of residuals of dependent variable
4.  Normality of residuals of dependent variable

## 2. Building the MLRs

### a. Zinc

```{r}
library(MASS)
library(car)

# Build a long model considering all predictors
zn_mod <- lm(log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g_std ~ log_Temp_C_std + pH_std + log_DOC_nM_std +
               log_Ca_nM_std + log_Mg_nM_std + log_Na_nM_std + log_K_nM_std +
               log_DIC_nM_std + log_SO4_nM_std + log_Zn_nM_std, data = dat)

# Step-wise selection of the most parsimonious model using AIC
step.zn_mod <- stepAIC(zn_mod, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)

# Get summary of model
zn_mod_summary <- summary(step.zn_mod)
zn_mod_summary
```

Variance inflation factors

```{r}
vif_coeff.zn <- vif(step.zn_mod)
vif_coeff.zn
```

Diagnostic plots

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))   # 2 rows, 2 columns
step.zn_mod_plots <- plot(step.zn_mod)
step.zn_mod_plots
```

Partial regression plots of log BLM parameters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# 1. Extract retained predictors from stepwise model
retained_vars <- names(coef(step.zn_mod))[-1]  # drop intercept

# 2. Function to get partial residuals for each predictor
get_partial_df <- function(model, data, var) {
  # Construct model formula terms
  all_terms <- attr(terms(model), "term.labels")
  other_terms <- setdiff(all_terms, var)
  
  # Get residuals of Y on all predictors except the variable of interest
  y_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = all.vars(formula(model))[1])
  y_resid <- resid(lm(y_formula, data = data))
  
  # Get residuals of X_var on all other predictors
  x_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = var)
  x_resid <- resid(lm(x_formula, data = data))
  
  df <- data.frame(
    predictor = x_resid,
    response = y_resid,
    variable = var
  )
  return(df)
}

# 3. Build combined dataset for all retained predictors
partial_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(retained_vars, get_partial_df, 
                                    model = step.zn_mod, data = dat))

# 4. Plot partial regression slopes
step.zn_mod_partial_slopes <-
  ggplot(partial_df, aes(x = predictor, y = response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") + #95% CI
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor (residuals)",
    y = "Response (residuals)",
    title = "Partial Regression Plots for Retained Predictors (Zn Model)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

step.zn_mod_partial_slopes
```

Create a summary table

```{r}
# 1. Create a data frame with raw beta coefficients (partial slopes)
summary_mlr_zn <- as.data.frame(summary(step.zn_mod)$coefficients)

# 2. Extract term names
summary_mlr_zn$Term <- rownames(summary_mlr_zn)

# 3. Reorder columns to put Term first
summary_mlr_zn <- summary_mlr_zn[, c("Term", setdiff(names(summary_mlr_zn), "Term"))]

# 4. Add model label
summary_mlr_zn$Model <- "Zinc"

# 5. Convert VIF values to data.frame for merging
vif_zn <- data.frame(
  Term = names(vif_coeff.zn),
  VIF = as.numeric(vif_coeff.zn),
  row.names = NULL
)

# 6. Merge the result with vif_zn
summary_zn <- merge(summary_mlr_zn, vif_zn, by = "Term", all.x = TRUE)

# 7. Add model statistics
zn_mod_summary <- summary(step.zn_mod)

rse <- zn_mod_summary$sigma
r2 <- zn_mod_summary$r.squared
adj_r2 <- zn_mod_summary$adj.r.squared
fstat <- zn_mod_summary$fstatistic[1]
fnum <- zn_mod_summary$fstatistic[2]
fden <- zn_mod_summary$fstatistic[3]
pval <- pf(fstat, fnum, fden, lower.tail = FALSE)

# 8. Create data frame with model statistics matching the structure of summary_zn
model_stats <- data.frame(
  Term = c("Residual standard error", "Multiple R-squared", "Adjusted R-squared", "F-statistic", "p-value"),
  Estimate = c(rse, r2, adj_r2, fstat, pval),
  `Std. Error` = NA,
  `t value` = NA,
  `Pr(>|t|)` = NA,
  Model = "Zinc",
  VIF = NA,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 9. Check and fix column name mismatches before combining

# 10. Scale both sets of column names
names(summary_zn) <- c(
  "Term", "Estimate", "Std. Error", "t value", "Pr(>|t|)", "Model", "VIF")
names(model_stats) <- c("Term", "Estimate", "Std. Error", "t value", "Pr(>|t|)", "Model", "VIF")

# 10. Combine coefficients and model stats
summary_zn_final <- rbind(summary_zn, model_stats)

# View
print(summary_zn_final)
```

Export to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_all_sites.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Zn MLR" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Zn MLR")
} 

# Write your new table 
writeData(wb, "Zn MLR", summary_zn_final)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_all_sites.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

```

## 3. Outlier Detection

### i. Zinc Bioavailability

```{r}
# 1. Get model diagnostics
model_diag_zn <- influence.measures(step.zn_mod)

# 2. Extract indices of influential points flagged by diagnostics
infl_points_zn <- which(apply(model_diag_zn$is.inf, 1, any))

# 3. Create a dataframe with their info
flagged_obs_zn <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = dat$Sample_ID[infl_points_zn],
  Fitted = fitted(step.zn_mod)[infl_points_zn],
  Residual = residuals(step.zn_mod)[infl_points_zn],
  Std_Residual = rstandard(step.zn_mod)[infl_points_zn],
  Leverage = hatvalues(step.zn_mod)[infl_points_zn],
  Cooks_D = cooks.distance(step.zn_mod)[infl_points_zn])

# View flagged observations
flagged_obs_zn
```

Determine whether these flagged observations are clustered around a certain characteristic

```{r}

### ---- By Typology ----

# 2b. Proportion of flagged by cluster
prop_typ_zn <- flagged_obs_zn %>%
  count(Typology) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 2c. Overall proportions in dataset
overall_typ_zn <- dat %>%
  count(Typology) %>%
  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 2d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_typ_zn <- left_join(prop_typ_zn, overall_typ_zn, by = "Typology")


### ---- By Site ----

# 3b. Proportion flagged per site

  count(Site) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 3c. Overall proportions in dataset

  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 3d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_site_zn <- left_join(prop_site_zn, overall_site_zn, by = "Site")


### ---- By Date ----

# 4b. Proportion flagged per date

  count(Date) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 4c. Overall proportions in dataset

  count(Date) %>%
  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 4d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_date_zn <- left_join(prop_date_zn, overall_date_zn, by = "Date")

# 5. Combine plots
library(dplyr)

compare_typ_zn2 <- compare_typ_zn %>%

compare_site_zn2 <- compare_site_zn %>%

combined_zn
```

# Assessing Variables by Typology

First, we'll import the the Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_3.xlsx and name it dat:

```{r}
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

head(dat)
```

```{r}
                          levels = c("Pooled Water",
```

## 1. Summary Statistics

Mean and standard error by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Standard error function
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
}

# Mode function (returns the most frequent value)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

summary_table <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, where(is.numeric)) %>%  # keep Typology + numeric vars
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean     = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median   = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mode     = get_mode(Value),
    Variance = var(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE       = se(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_table
```

## 2. Check of ANOVA Assumptions

To determine whether variables significantly differ by typology, we could use a parametric ANOVA which assumes variables are normally distributed and have homogeneity of variance by typology. We already determined that most variables were not normally distributed (**Preparing Variables** section), even after log-transforming them. Now we will assess homogeneity of variance by typology.

### a. Homogeneity of Variance

Using the Levene Test

```{r}
library(car)  # for leveneTest()
library(dplyr)

# Set alpha for homogeneity check
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify all numeric variables EXCEPT Typology
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
levene_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  F_value = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Homogeneous = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all numeric variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Run Levene's test
  test <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(var, "~ Typology")), data = dat)
  
  # Extract F and p-values
  F_val <- test[1, "F value"]
  p_val <- test[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  
  # Determine homogeneity
  homogeneous <- p_val > alpha
  
  # Add results to dataframe
  levene_results <- rbind(
    levene_results, 
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      F_value = F_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Homogeneous = homogeneous
    )
  )
}

# View results
levene_results
```

Most variables do not have homogeneous variance.

Export results to excel

```{r}
# Create sheet if it does NOT exist

  addWorksheet(wb, "Homog Var by Typology")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Homog Var by Typology", levene_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 3. Kruskal Wallis Test

Since most variables fail the assumptions for an ANOVA, we will use a non-parametric rank-based test to determine whether variables significantly differ by stream typology; the Kruskal Wallis (KW) test. We will also use the Holm-Bonferroni correction factor for multiple comparisons when conducting pairwise comparisons of variables by typology.

**Assumptions of the KW test** according to geeksforgeeks.org

1.  ***For ordinal, interval, or ratio data:*** While most of our variables fail this assumption, we can make an exception while being aware of this.

2.  ***The samples are independent of each other and within each group:*** Our variables meet this assumption.

3.  ***The distributions of the groups should have the same shape.***

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Choose variables whose distributions you want to compare by Typology
vars_to_check <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM",
  "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g_std",
  "log_Cu_nM",
  "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g_std",
  "log_Temp_C_std", 
  "pH_std", 
  "log_DOC_nM_std",
  "log_DIC_nM_std", 
  "log_Cl_nM_std", 
  "log_Ca_nM_std",
  "log_Mg_nM_std", 
  "log_SO4_nM_std", 
  "log_Na_nM_std",
  "log_K_nM_std"
)

# Change to long format
dat_long <- dat %>%
  # Keep Typology and the variables you want to check
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_to_check)) %>%
  
  # Turn columns into rows: Variable, Value
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Density plots by Typology
ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Value, fill = Typology)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +   # alpha for transparent fill
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free") +  # one panel per Variable
  labs(
    title = "Distributions by Typology",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

Generally, the distributions are similar by Typology for each Variable except for Ca, Cu, Zn, and DIC.

The KW test also can't handle variables with missing values and no variance, we'll check to see if any variables have these two conditions

```{r}
library(dplyr)

na_counts <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "NA_count") %>%
  filter(NA_count > 0)

na_counts
```

No variables have missing values, now we'll check for lack of variance

```{r}
no_variance <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~dplyr::n_distinct(., na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Distinct_values") %>%
  filter(Distinct_values <= 1)

no_variance
```

If there are variables with no variance, it's likely an error from running BLM.

Now we can perform the KW test

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(agricolae)
library(dplyr)

alpha <- 0.05

# 1. Get all numeric variables in dat
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# 2. Create an empty list to store rows
combined_list <- list()

# 3. Loop through each numeric variable 
i <- 1
for (v in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Kruskal-Wallis test
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ Typology"))
  kw_test <- kruskal.test(formula, data = dat)
  
  chi_sq     <- kw_test$statistic
  df_val     <- kw_test$parameter
  p_val      <- kw_test$p.value
  significant <- p_val < alpha   # significant when p < 0.05
  
  # agricolae::kruskal to assign groups (letters)
  k_out <- agricolae::kruskal(
    y    = dat[[v]],
    trt  = dat$Typology,
    alpha = alpha,
    group = TRUE
  )
  
  # Create a data frame from the groups table
  groups_df <- k_out$groups %>%
    rownames_to_column("Typology")
  
  # Combine test results with group letters
  combined_list[[i]] <- groups_df %>%
    mutate(
      Variable   = v,
      Chi_sq     = as.numeric(chi_sq),
      df         = as.numeric(df_val),
      p_value    = as.numeric(p_val),
      Significant = significant
    )
  
  i <- i + 1
}

# 5. Bind everything together
combined_kruskal <- bind_rows(combined_list)

# View
combined_kruskal
```

```{r}
}
```

```{r}
library(fBasics)
library(tibble)
library(agricolae)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "English_United States.UTF-8")


# 1. Titles for each variable's plot (panel title)
title_lookup <- c(
  "log_Temp_C" = "Temperature",
  "pH"         = "pH",
  "log_DOC_uM" = "Dissolved Organic Carbon",
  "log_DIC_uM" = "Dissolved Inorganic Carbon",
  "log_Ca_uM"  = "Calcium",
  "log_Mg_uM"  = "Magnesium",
  "log_Na_uM"  = "Sodium",
  "log_K_uM"   = "Potassium",
  "log_SO4_uM" = "Sulfate",
  "log_Cl_uM"  = "Chloride"
)

# 2. Custom y-axis labels for each variable
y_label_lookup <- c(
  "log_Temp_C" = "Temperature (°C)",
  "pH"         = "pH",
  "log_DOC_uM" = "log DOC (µM)",
  "log_DIC_uM" = "log DIC (µM)",
  "log_Ca_uM"  = "log Ca (µM)",
  "log_Mg_uM"  = "log Mg (µM)",
  "log_Na_uM"  = "log Na (µM)",
  "log_K_uM"   = "log K (µM)",
  "log_SO4_uM" = "log SO₄ (µM)",
  "log_Cl_uM"  = "log Cl (µM)"
)

# 3. Colors for each Typology abbreviation
typology_colors <- c(
  "Pooled Water"        = "#E69F00",
  "Tributaries"         = "#56B4E9",
  "Developed Tributaries" = "#D55E00",
  "Main Stem"           = "#999999"
)

# 4. Create output folder (if it doesn't exist)
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# 5. Loop through variables in title_lookup
for (var in names(title_lookup)) {

  # a) y-position for letters: e.g. 1.25 * max per Typology
  y_pos_df <- dat %>%
    group_by(Typology) %>%
    summarise(
      y_pos = max(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25,
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # b) SUBSET your letters table for this variable 
  #    letters_df must have columns: Variable, Typology, Letters
  letters_sub <- letters_df %>%
    filter(Variable == var) %>%
    dplyr::select(Typology, Letters)

  # c) JOIN letters with y positions
  letters_plot_df <- letters_sub %>%
    left_join(y_pos_df, by = "Typology")

  # d) Build ggplot
  p <- ggplot(dat, aes(
      x = Typology,
      y = .data[[var]],
      color = Typology
    )) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
    geom_jitter(
      width = 0.15,
      size = 2,
      alpha = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = letters_plot_df,
      aes(
        x = Typology,
        y = y_pos,
        label = Letters
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 5
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
    labs(
      title = title_lookup[[var]],
      y     = y_label_lookup[[var]],
      x     = ""
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 11, angle = 0, vjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
    )

  print(p)
}
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Typology colors (exactly as you specified)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
typology_colors <- c(
  "Pooled Water"          = "#E69F00",
  "Tributaries"           = "#56B4E9",
  "Developed Tributaries" = "#D55E00",
  "Main Stem"             = "#999999"
)

# 1. Make sure output folder exists
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

# 2. Put data into long format: one row = 1 observation of 1 variable
dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(names(title_lookup))) %>%  
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# 3. Prepare letters for all variables in one table ----

# 3a. Get max y per Variable x Typology from the long data
y_pos_df <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 3b. Subset letters_df to only the variables you are plotting
#     letters_df must have: Variable, Typology, Letters
letters_long <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% names(title_lookup)) %>%
  # join to get y_max for each Variable x Typology
  left_join(y_pos_df, by = c("Variable", "Typology")) %>%
  # position letters slightly above the max
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max * 1.05
  )

# 4. Facet labels using title_lookup
facet_labels <- as_labeller(title_lookup)

# 5. Build one faceted plot
all_vars_panel <- ggplot(dat_long, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Typology
  )) +
  # Boxplots
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  
  # Jittered points
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  
  # Letters from Kruskal groups
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long,
    aes(
      x     = Typology,
      y     = y_pos,
      label = Letters
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  # Typology colors
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  
  # Facet by Variable, with nice titles
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales  = "free_y",
    ncol    = 3,
    labeller = facet_labels
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "BLM Predictors by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log Concentration (µM)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

### c. Factors Affecting Zinc Bioavailability

#### i. Carbonates

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. Variable titles and (optional) y-axis labels
# ------------------------------------------------
title_lookup <- c(
  "log_ZnCO3_nM"  = "Zinc(II) Carbonate",
  "log_ZnHCO3_nM" = "Zinc(I) Bicarbonate"
)

# Custom y-axis labels (optional)
y_label_lookup <- c(
  "log_ZnCO3_nM"  = "log ZnCO3 (nM)",
  "log_ZnHCO3_nM" = "log ZnHCO3 (nM)"
)

vars_zn_spec <- names(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 1. Make sure output folders exist
# ------------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

zn_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Zn Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(zn_dir)) dir.create(zn_dir)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 2. Long-format data for these variables (use Typology)
# ------------------------------------------------
dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_zn_spec)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# ------------------------------------------------
# 3. Letters for these variables only (from letters_df)
# ------------------------------------------------

# 3a. Max y per Variable x Typology
y_pos_df <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 3b. Join letters with y positions
#     letters_df must have: Variable, Typology, Letters
letters_long <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_zn_spec) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + 0.5   # Letters above boxplots
  )

# ------------------------------------------------
# 4. Facet labels using title_lookup
# ------------------------------------------------
facet_labels <- as_labeller(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build faceted Zn speciation panel
# ------------------------------------------------
zn_speciation_panel <- ggplot(dat_long, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Typology
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  # use your full Typology palette
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales   = "free_y",
    ncol     = 3,
    labeller = facet_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Zinc Carbonate Speciation by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log Concentration (µM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# 6. Show in RStudio
zn_speciation_panel
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# ---------------------------------------------

  "log_Ca_nM"           = "Total Calcium",

)

# Optional: custom y-axis labels if you want later
zn_y_label_lookup <- c(
  "log_Ca_nM"           = "log Ca (nM)",
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g_Zn" = "log BL-Ca (nmol/g wet weight)"
)

vars_zn_spec <- names(zn_title_lookup)

# ---------------------------------------------
# 2. Output folder: Plots by Typology/Zn Speciation
# ---------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

zn_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Zn Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(zn_dir)) dir.create(zn_dir)

# ---------------------------------------------
# 3. Long-format data for Zn speciation variables (use Typology)
# ---------------------------------------------
dat_long_zn <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_zn_spec)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# ---------------------------------------------
# 4. Custom multipliers for letter height per variable
# ---------------------------------------------
letter_nudge_zn <- c(
  "log_Ca_nM"           = 0.2, 
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g_Zn" = 0.2
)

# ---------------------------------------------
# 5. Letters for Zn speciation variables (from letters_df)

  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 5b. Join letters with y positions
#     letters_df must have: Variable, Typology, Letters

  filter(Variable %in% vars_zn_spec) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df_zn,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # add a small offset instead of multiplying
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge_zn[Variable]
  )

  )) +

  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,

    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  # Letters from Kruskal groups
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_zn,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  # Typology colors (use your Typology palette)
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  # One facet per Zn variable
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales   = "free_y",
    ncol     = 2,
    labeller = facet_labels_zn
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Calcium Effects on Zinc Bioavailability",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log Concentration (nM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

#### v. Complexing Anions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. Variable titles for ZINC
# ------------------------------------------------
zn_title_lookup <- c(
  "log_ZnCO3_nM"  = "Zinc(II) Carbonate",
  "log_ZnHCO3_nM" = "Zinc(I) Bicarbonate"
)

zn_vars <- names(zn_title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 1. Output folders
# ------------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

zn_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Zn Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(zn_dir)) dir.create(zn_dir)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 2. Long-format zinc data (use Typology)
# ------------------------------------------------
zn_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(zn_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = zn_vars
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------
# 3. Letters for ZINC variables only
#    (includes 5 × y_mean placement with cap)
# ------------------------------------------------

# 3a. Compute group means for letter positioning
y_pos_df <- zn_long %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 3b. Attach y positions to letters_df (assumes Letters col exists)
letters_zn <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% zn_vars) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = zn_vars
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos_raw = y_mean * 5,
    y_pos     = ifelse(y_pos_raw > 3, 3 - 0.2, y_pos_raw)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------
# 4. Facet labels for zinc
# ------------------------------------------------
zn_facet_labels <- as_labeller(zn_title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build 2×2 ZINC speciation panel (shared y-axis)
# ------------------------------------------------
zn_speciation_panel <- ggplot(zn_long, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Typology
)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_zn,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    ncol    = 2,          # 2×2 layout
    scales  = "fixed",    # same axes across all panels
    labeller = zn_facet_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Zinc Carbonate Speciation by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "log Concentration (nM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# 6. Display
zn_speciation_panel

```

```{r}
)
```

### c. Factors Affecting Copper Bioavailability

#### i. Sulfate

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0. Name of the variable you want to plot
#-------------------------------------------------
var_name <- "log_CuSO4_uM"

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Titles and y-axis label for this variable
#-------------------------------------------------
title_var   <- "Copper Sulfate"
y_label_var <- "log CuSO₄ (µM)"

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Save to an output folder
#-------------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

cu_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Cu Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(cu_dir)) dir.create(cu_dir)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Letters for this variable only (from letters_df)
#-------------------------------------------------
letters_sub <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable == var_name)
# letters_df already has columns: Variable, Typology, Letters

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. y-position for letters: mean + constant offset
#-------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    y_pos = mean(.data[[var_name]], na.rm = TRUE) + 3,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# join y_pos into letters_sub by Typology
letters_sub <- letters_sub %>%
  left_join(y_pos_df, by = "Typology")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build ggplot for log_CuSO4_uM
#-------------------------------------------------
p_cuso4_cu <- ggplot(dat, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = .data[[var_name]],
    color = Typology
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 2,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_sub,
    aes(
      x = Typology,
      y = y_pos,
      label = Letters
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  labs(
    title = title_var,
    y     = y_label_var,
    x     = ""
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0. Name of the variable you want to plot
#-------------------------------------------------
var_name <- "log_TOrg_Cu_nM"   # or "log_Torg_Cu_nM" if that's the exact name

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Titles and y-axis label for this variable
#-------------------------------------------------
title_var   <- "Total Organic Copper"
y_label_var <- "log TOrg Cu (nM)"

# -----------------------------------------------
# 3. Save to an output folder
# -----------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

cu_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Cu Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(cu_dir)) dir.create(cu_dir)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Letters for this variable only (from letters_df)
#-------------------------------------------------
# letters_df has: Variable, Typology, Letters
letters_sub <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable == var_name)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. y-position for letters: 1.25 * max per Typology
#-------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    y_pos = max(.data[[var_name]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# join y_pos into letters_sub
letters_sub <- letters_sub %>%
  left_join(y_pos_df, by = "Typology")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Build ggplot for log_TOrg_Cu_nM
#-------------------------------------------------
p_torg_cu <- ggplot(dat, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = .data[[var_name]],
    color = Typology
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 2,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_sub,
    aes(
      x = Typology,
      y = y_pos,
      label = Letters
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  labs(
    title = title_var,
    y     = y_label_var,
    x     = ""
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. Variable titles and y-axis labels
# ------------------------------------------------
title_lookup <- c(
  "log_BL_Na_nmol_g_Cu"  = "Biotic Ligand-Bound Sodium",
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g_Cu"  = "Biotic Ligand-Bound Calcium"
)

# Custom y-axis labels (optional)
y_label_lookup <- c(
  "log_BL_Na_nmol_g_Cu"  = "log BL-Na (nM)",
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g_Cu"  = "log BL-Ca (nM)"
)

vars_zn_spec <- names(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 1. Make sure output folders exist
# ------------------------------------------------
output_dir <- "Plots by Typology"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir)

zn_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "Zn Speciation")
if (!dir.exists(zn_dir)) dir.create(zn_dir)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 2. Long-format data for these variables
# ------------------------------------------------
dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_zn_spec)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value))

# ------------------------------------------------
# 3. Letters for these variables only (from letters_df)
# ------------------------------------------------

# 3a. Max y per Variable x Typology
y_pos_df <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 3b. Join letters with y positions
#     letters_df has: Variable, Typology, Letters
letters_long <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_zn_spec) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + 0.5   # Letters above boxplots
  )

# ------------------------------------------------
# 4. Facet labels using title_lookup
# ------------------------------------------------
facet_labels <- as_labeller(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build faceted Cu competing cations panel
# ------------------------------------------------
cu_cc_panel <- ggplot(dat_long, aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Typology
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales   = "free_y",
    ncol     = 3,
    labeller = facet_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Copper Competing Cations by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log Concentration (µM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

Calculate the probability of Zn toxicity to daphnia by typology

```{r}
#Quantify overlapping area of measured zinc with toxic concentrations by typology

# Extract the two vectors
x1 <- dat$log_Zn_nM
x2 <- dat$log_Zn_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM

library(dplyr)

# --- Define overlap function ---
overlap_area <- function(x, y, n = 512) {
  d1 <- density(x, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  d2 <- density(y, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  
  x_start <- max(min(d1$x), min(d2$x))
  x_end   <- min(max(d1$x), max(d2$x))
  
  if(x_start >= x_end) return(0)  # No overlap
  
  x_common <- seq(x_start, x_end, length.out = n)
  y1 <- approx(d1$x, d1$y, x_common)$y
  y2 <- approx(d2$x, d2$y, x_common)$y
  
  sum(pmin(y1, y2)) * diff(x_common[1:2])
}


# --- Compute overlaps by Typology ---
overlap_Zn_by_typology <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Overlap_Daphnia = overlap_area(log_Zn_nM, log_Zn_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# View results
overlap_Zn_by_typology
```

Calculate probability of overlapping measured copper with toxic levels of copper by stream typology

```{r}
#Quantify overlapping area of measured copper with toxic concentrations by typology

# Extract the two vectors
x1 <- dat$log_Cu_nM
x2 <- dat$log_Cu_Chronic_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM
x3 <- dat$log_Cu_Acute_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM
x4 <- dat$log_Cu_Chronic_Toxicity_Minnow_nM
x5 <- dat$log_Cu_Acute_Toxicity_Minnow_nM

# Compute density overlaps between measured Cu and toxicity thresholds
library(dplyr)

overlap_area <- function(x, y, n = 512) {
  d1 <- density(x, n = n)
  d2 <- density(y, n = n)
  
  # Common x grid
  x_common <- seq(max(min(d1$x), min(d2$x)), min(max(d1$x), max(d2$x)), length.out = n)
  
  y1 <- approx(d1$x, d1$y, x_common)$y
  y2 <- approx(d2$x, d2$y, x_common)$y
  
  # Area under the minimum of both density curves
  overlap <- sum(pmin(y1, y2)) * diff(x_common[1:2])
  return(overlap)
}

# --- Compute overlaps by Typology ---
overlap_results_by_typology <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    
    Overlap_Chronic_Toxicity_Daphnia = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Chronic_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM),
    
    Overlap_Acute_Toxicity_Daphnia   = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Acute_Toxicity_Daphnia_nM),
    
    Overlap_Chronic_Toxicity_Minnow  = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Chronic_Toxicity_Minnow_nM),
    
    Overlap_Acute_Toxicity_Minnow    = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Acute_Toxicity_Minnow_nM)
  
    ) %>%
  ungroup()

# View
overlap_results_by_typology
```

```{r}
    x = "Site (grouped by network)",
    y = " Log TBL Cu (umol/g wet weight)"
  ) +
  theme_test() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  ) +

  # Add vertical dividers between networks
  facet_grid(~Network, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x")

# View 
f_tribs_plot_zn
f_tribs_plot_cu
```

Save to folder called Plots of Flowing Tributaries

```{r}
# Define output directory

if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {

)
```

## 4. Pooled Water

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Isolate typology and order the sites
pw_typology <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology == "Pooled Water") %>%
  mutate(Site = factor(Site, 
                       levels = unique(Site[order(Dist_from_EFPC_km)])))


# Plot by site colored by Network
library(ggplot2)

# Zinc
pooled_water_plot_zn <- ggplot(
  pw_typology, aes(x = Site, y = log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g, fill = Network)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  labs(
    title = "Bioavailable Zn in Pooled Water",
    x = "Site (grouped by network)",
    y = " Log TBL Zn (umol/g wet weight)"
  ) +
  theme_test() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  ) +

  # Add vertical dividers between networks
  facet_grid(~Network, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x")

# Copper
pooled_water_plot_cu <- ggplot(pw_typology, aes(x = Site, y = log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g, fill = Network)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  labs(
    title = "Bioavailable Cu in Pooled Water",
    x = "Site (grouped by network)",
    y = " Log TBL Cu (umol/g wet weight)"
  ) +
  theme_test() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  ) +

  # Add vertical dividers between networks
  facet_grid(~Network, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x")

# View 
pooled_water_plot_zn
pooled_water_plot_cu
```

```{r}
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Bioavailable_Zn_by_site.png"),

ggsave(
```
